speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you notice any red streaks spreading from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

Thank you for that detailed history; the one-month duration, the ant bite vector, your history of immunosuppression from uveitis treatment, and your diabetes are all significant risk factors. Given the ulcerative nature and your specific background, could you describe the current size of the lesion and whether the wound has an irregular or raised border?
